title.narrative: Enabling meaningful participation of citizens in climate change policy legislation and climate financing advocacy

description.narrative:
South Sudan is one of the most climate-vulnerable countries in the world, facing recurrent and intensifying climate shocks such as floods, droughts, and heatwave. These events have devastated livelihoods, displaced communities, and eroded local coping mechanisms, particularly affecting women, children, and marginalized groups. The impacts of climate change are compounded by weak governance structures, limited institutional capacity, and ongoing intercommunal conflicts over scarce natural resources. As a result, food insecurity, disease outbreaks, and environmental degradation are on the rise, creating a cycle of vulnerability and instability. Therefore, this project is justified by the urgent need to build local resilience through inclusive, community-driven, and faith-based approaches. By strengthening the capacity of civil society, faith-based organizations, and local authorities, the project will empower communities to adopt climate-smart practices, influence policy, and engage in sustainable natural resource management. Leveraging the moral authority of faith leaders and promoting gender-responsive solutions ensures that climate action is both locally rooted and socially inclusive. The project also addresses critical information and coordination gaps, fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration to drive long-term climate adaptation and mitigation in South Sudan. The overall objective of this project is to strengthen citizens’ meaningful participation in climate change policy legislation and the climate financing decision-making process in South Sudan.
Objective 1: To strengthen institutional capacity of local actors (faith-based organizations, CSOs, government bodies) to engage in climate governance and policy influence.
Objective 2: To enhance community awareness and participation in climate action through advocacy on environmental stewardship and awareness raising.
Objective 3: To foster multi-stakeholder collaboration for sustainable natural resource management and climate resilience Outcome 1: Increased capacity of 60% local institutions such as (CSOs, faith-based organisation, line Ministries etc.) to influence and implement climate policies and adaptation strategies. Output 1.1: Training programs conducted for CSOs, FBOs, and local authorities on climate governance and policy advocacy Outcome 2: Increased community awareness, collaboration between public, private, and faith-based actors in climate resilience and governance and active participation in climate action through inclusive advocacy, environmental education, and promotion of environmental stewardship. Output 2 .1: 4 Community awareness campaigns on climate financing and justice implemented
